title: The Lawson-Haggart band and its 30 albums
summary: Leeman calls the Yank Lawson-Bob Haggart band a mutual admiration society where he never had a bad night across nearly thirty albums.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: It was the Lawson-Haggart band which was another one of my great loves -- and I accomplished so many things with them. Everything was just -- everything turned to honey and cream in that orchestra. I can't ever

remember doing anything wrong with them -- they're not the epitome in drumming, but it was every time we got together, we never had a bad night, and I always looked forward to going out to concerts with them, which I do every year.

And that was another great -- which I did after Eddie Condon's -- the feeling inside, we did almost 30 or 31 albums with the Lawson-Haggard band, and still working on the outside, and it was nothing but a mutual admiration society. It was terrible on our record dates because we'd sit around like a bunch of jibbering fans enjoying ourselves, and that's an awful ego trip.

But I don't know if the kids can get that today, if they go to NBC and do a night, and with all that amplification, they must. They just must inside, have a feeling of satisfaction on some nights that they get together. Although I'm not into that music. If they're having problems, I'd be happy to -- I've met guys in New York who do shows, good shows, that are also swingers. You know Marcus around the corner.
